transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, nice to meet you too. I came in because... I don't know, I just can’t shake this feeling lately at work. I'm a secondary school teacher, and recently the staff emails and the morning announcements... I feel like they are actually coded messages about me. 

Which is funny because the intercom speaker in my classroom has this awful buzzing sound. I asked the custodian, Gary, to look at it, but he’s always so busy with the new recycling program they just started. They want us to separate the glossy paper from the matte paper now, which seems a bit excessive to me, but I suppose the district has its reasons. My husband is the exact same way with organizing his workbench in the garage, he has all these little jars for screws... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the emails. My colleagues have been very sweet about it, and they gently show me that the messages are just standard memos sent to everyone on the staff list. But when I read them, or hear those morning announcements, I still just get this overwhelming feeling that there's a hidden meaning in there meant specifically for me.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or especially energized lately?

Energized? No, not really. I haven't felt high or anything like that. I mean, my energy is just... average, I suppose. Though, speaking of energy, the kids this semester are just bouncing off the walls. I have the ninth graders right after lunch, and I swear they must be eating pure sugar in the cafeteria. They used to serve those little fruit cups, but they swapped them for these packaged cookies to save money. I brought one home to my husband once, and he said it tasted like cardboard. He's very particular about his baked goods, ever since we went to that little bakery in Vermont... oh, it was a beautiful trip, the leaves were just turning that bright orange. We stayed in this quaint little bed and breakfast that had these gorgeous antique quilts. 

But... I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my energy. No, I haven't felt unusually energized at all.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Voices? Well, yes, actually. Sometimes when I'm at home, or after the bell rings and the classroom finally empties out... it gets so quiet. I always liked the quiet, though. My mother used to say silence is golden, which is funny because she loved to play the radio all day long. She had this old wooden Zenith radio that she kept right on the kitchen counter, and she'd listen to these local talk shows while she was making dinner. She made the most wonderful pot roast, with those little pearl onions and baby carrots. I've tried to replicate her recipe for years, but my husband says it's never quite the same. Maybe it's the type of beef I'm buying... the butcher down at our local supermarket retired last month, and the new guy just doesn't trim the fat the way I like. He's a nice enough young man, always asks about my garden, but... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, hearing things. Yes, in that quiet, whether I'm at home or in the empty classroom, I'll hear a woman's voice. She just says my name, or makes a short little comment about whatever it is I'm doing at that moment. It sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer her out loud—like I'll say, "I'm just organizing these folders!"—before I look up and realize there is absolutely no one else in the room with me.
Have you had any recent medical or neurological illness, like a seizure, head injury, or brain infection?

Medical illness? No, nothing like that. No seizures or head injuries or anything. I haven't been to the hospital in years, actually. The last time was when I had my gallbladder out, and oh, that was an ordeal. The hospital food was just dreadful. They brought me this gelatin that was supposed to be cherry-flavored, but it tasted exactly like cough syrup. My husband tried to sneak in some proper food—he brought a sandwich from that little deli near the train station, the one with the green awning? They make their own rye bread, it's so thick and crusty. We used to go there every Sunday after church when the kids were little, before they built that big shopping center across the street and ruined the parking. Now you have to park three blocks away just to get a decent pastrami on rye... 

I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, medical problems. No, my health has been fine. No brain infections or anything like that.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day lately?

Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't been feeling sad or down most of the day. I mean, the weather lately has been a bit gloomy, which always makes the classroom feel a little dreary in the afternoons. I actually tried putting up some new bulletin board borders to brighten the place up—these lovely yellow scalloped ones. I bought them at that teacher supply store over on 4th Street. They used to have such a wonderful selection of construction paper, just every color you could possibly imagine. Now it's all just pre-packaged kits and it's so flimsy. It's a shame, really. I remember when my daughter was in kindergarten, she made this beautiful hand-turkey out of this vibrant orange paper that they just don't make anymore. We still have it taped to the inside of the pantry door. The tape is completely yellowed and peeling now, of course. I really need to clean out that pantry this weekend, I'm pretty sure I have cans of tomato soup from three years ago sitting all the way in the back... 

Oh, I'm sorry, my mind is wandering again. What was the question? Oh, right, about being depressed. No, I haven't been feeling depressed at all.
How long have you been hearing that woman's voice?

How long? Oh, let me think. It started right around the time we had the midterm grading period. Grading always takes so much out of me, sitting at the dining room table with a pen for hours. Though I actually switched to purple pens a few years ago. Red just seems so aggressive, don't you think? The students respond much better to purple. I buy them in bulk from this little stationery shop downtown. The owner, Mr. Abernathy, he's been running that shop since I was a little girl. He has this beautiful antique brass cash register that still rings with a real bell. It's so rare to see craftsmanship like that these days. Everything now is just plastic and touch screens. My husband bought one of those new smart refrigerators with a screen on it, and I swear it's more complicated than teaching algebra. I just want it to keep the milk cold, I don't need it to tell me the weather in Tokyo or play music... 

Oh dear, I'm so sorry, I've completely lost the thread again. What were you asking? Oh, how long the voice has been there. Right. Well, the voice I sometimes answer, and I suppose those worries I've been having about the coded messages, too... they've both been happening for about four months now.
Do people tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that you go off track a lot when you talk?

Hard to follow? Oh, no, I don't think so. My students usually say I explain things very clearly. Especially when we cover the Renaissance period. There's just so much rich detail there, you know? Like the Medici family—I was actually watching a program about them on PBS just the other night. The way they practically invented modern banking is just fascinating. It actually reminded me that I still need to run to the bank to deposit a birthday check from my sister. She always sends it in one of those lovely handmade cards with the pressed flowers on the front. She buys them from a little artisan shop up in Vermont near her summer cabin. We used to spend our summers up there when we were girls, just catching minnows in the shallows with these little plastic buckets. The water was always absolutely freezing, even in the middle of July... 

Oh, dear. I've completely lost my place again. I am so sorry. You were asking if people say I go off track? Well... I suppose I do tend to wander a bit when I'm telling a story, but no, no one has ever complained that my speech is hard to follow or anything like that.
Since these experiences began, have they ever gone away completely for a full month?

Gone away completely? Let me think about that. A full month... Well, time has just been flying by lately, hasn't it? It feels like we just finished the spring semester, and now we're already looking at the fall schedule. The administration is completely overhauling the bell schedule next year, which is just going to be a nightmare for the bus routes. They want to start first period ten minutes earlier, which doesn't sound like much, but when you have teenagers trying to get out the door... My son used to be impossible to wake up when he was that age. I'd have to go in there and physically pull the blankets off him. He had this awful plaid comforter that he refused to wash because he said it would ruin the "perfect softness." Teenagers are so particular about the strangest things. Now he's an accountant in Chicago and wears a suit every day, if you can believe it. He called me last Sunday to tell me about his new espresso machine. Apparently, it grinds the beans right there in the machine, which sounds terribly loud for an apartment building...

Oh, goodness. I'm so sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? My mind just goes. You were asking if they ever went away for a whole month. No, no, I don't think they have. It's been pretty constant since it all started.

During these past four months, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling the messages were about you, but you were not depressed or unusually high at all?

Depressed or unusually high? Let me think... well, my mood always fluctuates a bit with the weather, to be honest. It's been so incredibly dreary lately, hasn't it? The rain just hasn't stopped since Tuesday. I actually had to buy a new umbrella because I left my good one on the train. It was one of those sturdy golf umbrellas, the kind with the double canopy so it doesn't flip inside out in the wind. My husband bought it for me when we went to Scotland for our anniversary a few years ago. Such a beautiful country, even though I don't play golf at all. I just walked along the coast while he played and collected these lovely, smooth pieces of sea glass. I keep them in a little mason jar on my classroom windowsill. The sunlight hits the green and blue glass just perfectly right around three o'clock, right when the final bell rings... 

Oh, goodness me. I am so sorry, my mind is just wandering all over the place today. You were asking about my mood, if I was depressed or high for two weeks while the voice was there? You know, I'm really not sure. I haven't really kept track of my moods like that, to be honest. I just haven't noticed if there was a specific two-week block like you're saying.
Over the past few months, have you found yourself talking much less than usual?

Talking less? Well... I suppose I have been. I still care about my students and my friends, of course I do, but it just feels like all the warmth and drive have completely drained out of me for months now. I used to be so involved, you know? The book club, the theater planning committee... we were supposed to do 'Our Town' this spring. Such a classic. I remember when I played Emily Webb in high school. My mother made my costume from this beautiful white eyelet cotton she found at a discount fabric store. The store was owned by this sweet older couple who always had a bowl of butterscotch candies on the counter. I can still smell that place—it smelled like dust and peppermint and old paper. They had these massive rolls of velvet in the back that I was never allowed to touch... 

Oh, dear. I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry. You were asking if I'm talking less. Yes, I suppose I am. I just let everything slide—the book club, the theater, even just simple phone calls. I just don't do it unless someone really pushes me to.
During these four months, was there ever a time when the voice or the coded-message feeling was happening, but your mood felt completely normal?

Completely normal? Well... I suppose I always try to keep things feeling as normal as possible. I actually have a little sign on my desk at school that says "Normal is just a setting on the washing machine." One of my homeroom students gave it to me years ago. Which actually reminds me, my own washing machine has been making this dreadful clanking noise during the spin cycle all week. It's one of those newer front-loading ones. They're supposed to be so much better for the environment, saving water and all that, but you absolutely have to leave the door open after a load or the whole drum smells terribly like mildew. My neighbor, Susan, she actually had to rip up her entire laundry room floor because her front-loader leaked while she was visiting her sister in Arizona. Sedona, I think it was. She said the red rocks were just breathtaking at sunrise. She brought me back this tiny little cactus in a hand-painted pot, and I've somehow managed to keep it alive for three years...

Oh, for heaven's sake. I am so sorry. I'm doing it yet again, aren't I? My brain is just taking the scenic route today. You were asking if my mood felt completely normal while the voice and the messages were happening. Honestly, I really couldn't say. I just haven't been paying close enough attention to my moods to know if they were ever perfectly normal while all the rest of it was going on. I'm just not sure.
Altogether, since these problems first began, has it been at least six months?

Six months? Oh, it's definitely been longer than that. It really started right around the time my youngest left for college. He went up to this lovely little liberal arts school in Vermont. The drive up there for move-in day was just spectacular, the leaves were just barely starting to turn that beautiful golden color. We stopped at this tiny diner off the interstate that had the most incredible blueberry pancakes. Real maple syrup, too, not that artificial corn syrup stuff they sell in the plastic bottles at the grocery store. I always tell my students—well, they call the class Family and Consumer Sciences now, not Home Ec—that you can always, always taste the difference when you use authentic ingredients. We actually made a beautiful quiche lorraine in class last week, though one of the boys accidentally used salt instead of sugar for the crust and... 

Oh, goodness. I am so sorry, I've done it again. My mind just keeps taking these little detours today. You were asking about how long it's been. Yes, it's been about a year and two months ago, since he moved into his dorm. That's really when this overall change in how I think, how I work, and how I connect with people all began.
Since all of this began, have you ever had a period when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Depressed nearly every day for two weeks? Well... I suppose I haven't really had that. I mean, I've had my down days, sure, but not a solid two weeks of feeling depressed every single day. I usually try to keep busy, you know? Keeping busy is the best medicine, my grandmother used to say. She was a remarkable woman. Raised six children during the Depression on a farm in Ohio. She used to tell us stories about how they would make clothes out of flour sacks. Can you imagine? The flour companies actually started printing pretty floral patterns on the sacks when they realized the women were using them for dresses. I always thought that was such a clever piece of marketing. I actually showed some pictures of those flour sack dresses to my students during our unit on textile history. The girls were just fascinated. One of them, Chloe, she's so talented, she actually went to a thrift store and bought some vintage feed sacks to make a skirt for her final project...

Oh, dear. I'm so sorry. I'm wandering off again, aren't I? I really don't mean to. You were asking about feeling depressed for two weeks straight. No, I don't think I've had anything like that. Just the usual ups and downs, I suppose, but nothing that lasted that long without a break.
Since this started, have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Much less sleep? Oh, heavens no. I've always been someone who absolutely needs my full eight hours. Though, I will say, getting a good night's rest has been a bit of a challenge since we bought that new memory foam mattress. My husband insisted on it after reading about it in a magazine. He refuses to read things on a tablet, always has to have the paper copy. Anyway, the mattress was supposed to have this special cooling gel, but I swear it just traps all the body heat. It's like trying to sleep inside a baked potato. I was actually just complaining about it in the teachers' lounge on Tuesday, and Mr. Harrison—he teaches AP Biology—he started explaining the thermal properties of polyurethane foam. He's always doing that, breaking every little thing down into science. Just yesterday he gave me this ten-minute lecture on the exact lactic acid bacteria needed for sourdough starters, which was actually quite helpful, really, because my third-period foods class has been having the hardest time getting our yeast to activate. The windows in the old wing of the building are so terribly drafty, you see, and...

Oh, for crying out loud. I am so sorry. I'm just rambling again, aren't I? I don't know why my thoughts keep drifting off into the weeds today. You asked if I had periods of needing less sleep but still feeling full of energy. No, definitely not. If I miss out on sleep, I feel it the next day just like anyone else. I certainly haven't had any unusual bursts of energy like that.
Have you felt emotionally flat or like it’s been hard to feel things, even with people or activities you used to care about?

Emotionally flat... well, I wouldn't say I don't care anymore. I still care very much about my students and my friends. But... yes, it has felt like the warmth and the drive have just sort of drained right out of me for many months now. It's so strange. I used to be the one organizing the neighborhood book club. We were reading this fascinating biography of Eleanor Roosevelt—did you know she actually wrote a daily syndicated newspaper column for over twenty years? It was called "My Day," and she wrote about everything from her travels to civil rights issues. I always thought that took such incredible discipline, to sit down and write every single day, no matter where she was or what she was doing. I try to get my students to keep a daily journal in my class, just a little reflection on what we cooked or sewed, but getting teenagers to write a paragraph a day is like pulling teeth. One boy, Tyler, he just draws little cartoons of vegetables in his journal instead of writing. He actually drew a very good caricature of a broccoli floret wearing a top hat last week, which I had to admit was quite clever, even if it wasn't the assignment...

Oh, goodness gracious. There I go again. I am so sorry, I don't know why I keep doing this. I just lose the thread of the conversation so easily today. You were asking about feeling emotionally flat. Yes, the drive is just gone. I let the book club go, and the theater planning committee at school... I don't even make simple phone calls anymore unless someone really pushes me to do it. It's just too much effort.
For at least one month, have you been going off track like this in conversations most days?

Going off track... well, I suppose I have been doing that a lot lately, haven't I? I didn't really notice it until you pointed it out, but my husband did mention something the other day. We were talking about the grocery list, and somehow I ended up telling him all about the new cashier at the supermarket. She's a lovely young girl, just started college, studying marine biology. I always find that so fascinating. I actually wanted to be a marine biologist when I was a little girl, after we took a family trip to Florida and saw the manatees. They are such gentle creatures, you know? They just float around eating sea grass all day. They call them sea cows, which I always thought was a bit uncharitable, considering how graceful they can be in the water. We took a glass-bottom boat tour, and the guide was this older gentleman who had lived on the coast his entire life... 

Oh, dear. I'm doing it right this second, aren't I? I am so sorry. You asked if I've been going off track like this most days for a month. I... I'm really not sure how long it's been happening, to be perfectly honest. I haven't really kept track of it. It just sort of happens without me realizing it.
